chini-mosque-saidpur.desc: The Chini Mosque was founded in the 19th century and later rebuilt and expanded by the local community. Its walls are covered in mosaic made of broken porcelain plates and glass, set in floral and geometric patterns that sparkle in the sun. Several small towers and domes rise above the facade. It is a cheerful, unusual building and the best-known sight in Saidpur.
blocks: How to get there
In Saidpur town, which has an airport with flights from Dhaka and a railway station; take a rickshaw to the mosque.
Good to know
Dress modestly and avoid prayer times. Midday sun shows the mosaic at its brightest.

glance: 355 km to Nilphamari by road, 9–12 hours by bus or car
teesta-barrage.desc: Completed around 1990, the Teesta Barrage spans the river between Dalia in Nilphamari's Dimla upazila and Doani in Lalmonirhat. It diverts water into canals that irrigate large areas of the northern districts. Visitors come to walk the approach roads and watch the water pour through the gates, especially in the rainy season when the river runs high. In the dry season the riverbed shows wide stretches of sand, telling its own story about water sharing in the region.
blocks: How to get there
From Nilphamari town or Saidpur, take a bus or CNG to Dalia in Dimla upazila.
Good to know
Some areas near the gates are restricted; follow guards' instructions. Evenings are pleasant on the embankment.

glance: Bus stands and markets in Nilphamari and Dimla
nilphamari-char-peanuts.desc: When the Teesta drops in the dry season, its sandy chars become fields, and peanuts are one of the main crops. Farmers in Dimla and nearby upazilas harvest them in late winter and spring. Roasted in hot sand in iron pans, the nuts are sold by the paper cone at markets and bus stands. They are a simple taste of the river's working landscape.
blocks: Good to know
Buy them hot from the roasting pan.

glance: 355 km to Nilphamari by road, 9–12 hours by bus or car
dharmapal-garh.desc: In the countryside of Jaldhaka upazila are the remains of a fortified enclosure, its earth walls and moat now covered with trees and fields. Local tradition connects it with a king called Dharmapal, and the ruins of his palace are said to lie on the bank of a small river to the east. Little has been excavated, and the site is more atmosphere than monument. It suits travellers who enjoy local legends and village walks.
blocks: How to get there
Take a bus to Jaldhaka from Nilphamari, then an auto-rickshaw; ask locally for Dharmapaler Garh.
Good to know
Go with a local guide, as there are no signs.

glance: 355 km to Nilphamari by road, 9–12 hours by bus or car
nilsagar.desc: Nilsagar is a large historic dighi in the countryside south-west of Nilphamari town. Local tradition links it with the legendary King Virat of the Mahabharata, and it was long known as Birat Dighi. Its wide banks are planted with trees and paths, and in winter migratory ducks gather on the water.
blocks: How to get there
About 14 km from Nilphamari town; take a CNG or auto-rickshaw.
Good to know
Come in the morning in winter for birds; keep your distance so they are not disturbed.

saidpur-railway-heritage.desc: Saidpur's railway workshop was set up in 1870 and became the largest in the country, repairing and rebuilding locomotives and carriages. Around it grew a planned colonial town of brick quarters, churches, clubs and markets, and communities from across the subcontinent came to work here. Generations of families have worked in the workshop, and railway culture still shapes daily life. Walking the old railway colony gives a sense of this layered history.
blocks: How to get there
The workshop and railway colony are in the heart of Saidpur town.
Good to know
Entering the workshop needs official permission; the colony streets can be explored freely.

saidpur-street-food.desc: Saidpur grew as a railway town and is home to a large Urdu-speaking community whose families came from Bihar and other parts of India. Their cooking adds a distinctive flavour to the north, with seekh kebabs, rich nihari and paya, and freshly baked breads. In the evenings, small eateries and street stalls in the town centre fill with the smoke of grills. It is a food culture quite different from the surrounding villages.
blocks: Good to know
Go hungry in the evening; ask locals which stall is busiest.

harishchandra-path.desc: Harishchandra's Path is a protected archaeological site in Khutamara union of Jaldhaka upazila, named after a king remembered locally as a great giver. Folk plays and songs of the area tell of his daughters and their marriage to King Gopichandra. Today the site looks like a low earthen mound scattered with old bricks and stones, said to be the remains of a Shiva temple the king left unfinished at his death. Villagers believe no one should carry away even a brick from here. A Shiva temple nearby holds three festivals a year that draw crowds.
blocks: How to get there
From Nilphamari town take a bus or CNG to Jaldhaka, then an auto to Harishchandra Path village in Khutamara union.
Good to know
Leave every brick and stone where it lies, both out of respect for local belief and because it is a protected site. Dharmapal's Fort is in the same upazila.
